section_summary.extract_value: This abstract describes a study involving 143 undergraduate women who completed self-reports on exercise behavior, body orientation, body appreciation, and body-related talk. The results indicated that conversations about exercise and weight loss/dieting differentially predicted body appreciation. Specifically, the relationship between talk type and body appreciation was explained by the object–process dichotomy, with exercise conversations predicting body appreciation through considering what bodies can do, and weight loss/dieting conversations being mediated by negative body attitudes.
